course.name: Machine Learning: from data to decisions
course.description: Build, evaluate and explain reliable machine-learning models. Fourteen of twenty syllabus topics have been taught.
objectives: Frame supervised learning problems and audit dataset quality
Build reproducible preprocessing and supervised learning pipelines
Choose evaluation metrics and validation strategies without leakage
Explain model complexity, uncertainty and evidence-based next steps

materials.title: ML workflow and problem framing - class reference
materials.content: Frame a prediction problem by identifying the target, feature availability, unit of observation and evaluation objective. Separate supervised classification and regression from unsupervised exploration. A baseline must precede tuning; choose a metric tied to the actual decision.

materials.title: Data quality and missing values - class reference
materials.content: Inspect schema, missingness, duplicate entities and class balance before modeling. Missing values can have meaning; fit imputation only on the training fold. Dropping rows indiscriminately can change the target population. Record data-quality assumptions.

materials.title: Exploratory statistics - class reference
materials.content: Summarize numerical features with distributions, medians, quantiles and spread. Inspect outliers and groups; correlation alone does not establish causality. Compare distributions across train and test partitions without fitting transformations on held-out data.

materials.title: Probability and uncertainty - class reference
materials.content: Conditional probability expresses an event under observed information. Base rates affect interpretation of classifier outputs. Separate a model score from a calibrated probability and distinguish uncertainty caused by small samples from an observed model failure.

materials.title: Train / validation / test splits - class reference
materials.content: Keep the test set untouched until final evaluation. Use validation data or cross-validation for model and hyperparameter selection. Stratify suitable classification splits; preserve time order for forecasting and keep repeated entities in a single partition.

materials.title: Scaling, encoding and leakage - class reference
materials.content: Fit scalers, imputers and encoders only on training data. Apply the fitted transformation to held-out data using a pipeline. Leakage happens when information unavailable at prediction time influences training or validation, including preprocessing before splitting.

materials.title: Linear regression - class reference
materials.content: Linear regression predicts a continuous target using a weighted combination of features. Compare against a mean baseline, inspect residuals, and check whether relationships and evaluation assumptions are appropriate. Coefficients do not prove causal effects.

materials.title: MAE, RMSE and R-squared - class reference
materials.content: MAE uses absolute residuals in target units; RMSE penalizes large residuals more strongly. R-squared compares residual error to a constant baseline and can be negative. Compare metrics on the same held-out data and avoid selecting a model using training error.

materials.title: Logistic regression - class reference
materials.content: Logistic regression models a binary outcome with a linear decision function and a sigmoid mapping. The decision threshold converts scores into class labels. Feature scaling and regularization affect fitting; probabilities should be checked for calibration when needed.

materials.title: Precision, recall, F1 and ROC - class reference
materials.content: Compute precision as TP/(TP+FP), recall as TP/(TP+FN), and F1 as their harmonic mean. Choose metrics for error costs and class balance. Accuracy can hide failure on a rare class. Threshold changes alter precision and recall; ROC-AUC is not accuracy.

materials.title: Nearest-neighbor models - class reference
materials.content: K-nearest neighbors predicts from nearby training examples. Distance depends on feature scale, so fit preprocessing within training folds. Choose k using validation; small k can overfit and larger k smooths predictions. Training data and distance choice affect inference cost.

materials.title: Decision trees - class reference
materials.content: Decision trees partition feature space with rules chosen to improve an objective. Deep trees can fit noise. Control complexity with depth, leaf size or pruning and evaluate on held-out data. Feature importance alone is not causal evidence.

materials.title: Cross-validation and model selection - class reference
materials.content: Cross-validation repeats training and validation on distinct folds to estimate generalization. Fit the complete pipeline within each fold. Use stratification, groups or time-aware splitting as appropriate. Keep a final test set separate from model selection and report variability.

materials.title: Overfitting and regularization - class reference
materials.content: Regularization penalizes model complexity to reduce overfitting. Ridge uses L2 and lasso uses L1 penalties; scale numerical features appropriately. Choose penalty strength using cross-validation rather than the final test set. Compare training and validation behavior.
